strings.name: Indra Nooyi
strings.summary: Indra Nooyi studied science and management in India and the United States and worked in consulting and industrial strategy before joining PepsiCo. She was CEO from 2006 to 2018 and stepped down as chair in 2019. She pursued portfolio and long-term strategy changes, setting nutrition, environmental and workforce goals under Performance with Purpose, while tensions between food-and-beverage growth and public health remained. Afterward, she worked in board governance and wrote about women’s careers and caregiving.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach a November 2026 podcast release. Her CEO service ended in 2018 and chairmanship in 2019. Corporate nutrition and environmental goals are reported as goals, and portfolio changes are not proof of public-health outcomes.
strings.influence.rationale: Led PepsiCo over many years, reshaping its product portfolio and contributing to debates about corporate governance and women's leadership.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Reshaping consumer-business strategy
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Led changes to PepsiCo’s portfolio, linking performance with nutrition, environmental and workforce goals; goals are not independently verified health outcomes.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Women’s leadership and caregiving
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: An immigrant from India who became a major-company CEO, she later used her memoir to discuss careers, family and social support.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses transformation and board governance
strings.timeline.event-01.text: A newly released podcast conversation covered business change, board responsibilities in the AI era and the coexistence of work and family.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes My Life in Full
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Her memoir recounted her career from India to the United States and discussed work, family and caregiving support.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Steps down as PepsiCo chair
strings.timeline.event-03.text: After the CEO handover, left the chairmanship and board, ending her long leadership tenure at PepsiCo.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Ends her tenure as PepsiCo CEO
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Ramon Laguarta succeeded her as CEO, while she temporarily remained chair to support the leadership transition.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Becomes PepsiCo CEO
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Moved from finance and strategy leadership to CEO and advanced the long-term Performance with Purpose strategy.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Becomes president and CFO
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Took responsibility for group finance and corporate strategy and joined the board before later becoming CEO.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Joins PepsiCo
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Joined PepsiCo to lead strategic planning after work at Boston Consulting Group, Motorola and ABB.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completes her Yale management degree
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Earned a Master of Public and Private Management and then joined Boston Consulting Group to work on corporate strategy.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Moves to the US to study at Yale
strings.timeline.event-09.text: After beginning product-management work in India, moved to Connecticut for further business education.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Earns an IIM Calcutta management degree
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Completed her MBA in India and entered corporate product-management roles.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Graduates from Madras Christian College
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Completed science studies involving physics, chemistry and mathematics before pursuing management education.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Madras
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born and raised in Madras, India, in a family that valued education, before developing a career across India and the United States.
